question.text: Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS) has a statutory lock-in period of:

explanation.text: The Logic: ELSS has a statutory lock-in of 3 years. A minimum of 80% of the corpus must be invested in equity and equity-related instruments. Investments in ELSS qualify for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year, and this tax benefit is available only under the old income tax regime. The Trap: 5 years is the lock-in for solution-oriented retirement / children's funds, not ELSS. 1 year and 2 years are not statutory lock-in periods recognised by the SEBI categorisation framework for ELSS. Note: The 3-year lock-in applies separately to each instalment in an ELSS SIP — every SIP contribution is locked in for 3 years from the date it is invested.
